data.name: PermissionsRulesDescription
data.value: A rule that refuses always wins. Otherwise the last matching rule decides. An allow rule skips the question, but it never takes a call out of the sandbox or into a protected folder. Use * for any text and ? for one character. In a path, * stays inside one folder and ** crosses folders. An MCP tool rule matches the server name and tool name joined as server/tool. A rule that refuses a file path also hides those files from listing and search. In a sandboxed shell command they are kept out of reach when the command starts, so they look empty or unreadable. This covers an exact path anywhere, and a wildcard pattern inside the working folder and the folders you approved. It is best effort: the shell can still read a refused file from git history, a file created later is not covered, on macOS renaming a folder above a refused file may get around it, and a command with Unrestricted access is not sandboxed. Shell commands don't run if a rule matches too many files, if a ** rule would have to scan a very large folder, or if this system's sandbox can't hide a single file. A rule such as secrets/** or *.pem stays quick.
